long_biography.plain_text:
An integrated operating model defines the company Hess built: its own teams develop, manufacture and lay durable floor systems across food-processing, pharmaceutical, aeronautical and other demanding facilities. Combining material production with direct project delivery gave him a platform wider than a conventional contracting practice and placed technical improvement alongside field execution.

The pivotal shift came after the enterprise posted losses in 2003. Hess undertook a buyout of Louis Kaufman, relocated the administrative centre to Indianapolis and gained operational authority when their stock transaction completed two years later. Cornerstone eventually established its base in Brownsburg, where Hess remains founder and owner. Neither the valuation of his holding nor the firm’s private finances is disclosed, so the operating asset—not an estimated fortune—best explains his commercial position.
